/bench/repo/docs/plans/2026-03-24-user-resource-identifiers/design.md:Introduce a single canonical user-name builder in the v1 API layer that serializes `users/{username}` from resolved user data, and route every public user-name emitter through it. This satisfies the first design goal and aligns the public resource shape with `AIP-122: Resource names`.
/bench/repo/docs/plans/2026-03-24-user-resource-identifiers/design.md:Introduce a shared user-token resolver in `server/router/api/v1` that extracts the `users/{token}` segment, validates it as a username-form resource token, resolves the corresponding `store.User`, and then passes the resolved internal ID into permission checks and storage lookups. The fileserver's current `getUserByIdentifier` behavior shows both lookup styles exist today, but the API-layer contract for this issue becomes username-only rather than dual-mode.
/bench/repo/docs/plans/2026-03-24-user-resource-identifiers/design.md:Keep child resource tokens unchanged and only change the user segment. For names such as `users/{user}/settings/{setting}`, `users/{user}/webhooks/{webhook}`, `users/{user}/notifications/{notification}`, `users/{user}/shortcuts/{shortcut}`, and `users/{user}/personalAccessTokens/{token}`, the parent `user` token is resolved from the username, while the child token keeps its existing format and storage mapping. The analysis is complete. The delivery function, SSRF protection mechanism, and relevant file paths are ready.

Content-change triggers dispatch via `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` in `memo_update_helpers.go`, which calls `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` and then `webhook.PostAsync`. The actual HTTP POST runs inside `Post()` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`, where four background workers consume an `asyncPostQueue` and invoke `safeClient.Do(req)`. SSRF protection is enforced by two layers.

Registration-time validation lives in `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go`. It performs a DNS lookup and rejects addresses matched by `isReservedIP`.

Delivery-time protection uses `safeDialContext` on the HTTP transport. It re-resolves hostnames at dial time and blocks reserved IPs via `isReservedIP`. This prevents DNS rebinding.

The core `isReservedIP` check matches against `reservedCIDRs` including 127.0.0.0/8, RFC1918 ranges, link-local, and IPv6 equivalents.

A bypass exists through the `AllowPrivateIPs` flag, enabled by the `--allow-private-webhooks` option in `cmd/memos/main.go`.
